description: Install AWS SDK packages, update .gitignore, create .env.local.example, and create all AWS lib helper files (lib/dynamodb.ts, lib/s3.ts, lib/ses.ts, lib/cognito.ts). These are the foundational dependencies that FEAT-002 and FEAT-003 require.
steps: Step 1 — Install pinned AWS SDK packages from project root c:\Users\laksh\OneDrive\Attachments\Desktop\LumaPath: `npm install @aws-sdk/client-dynamodb@3.620.0 @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb@3.620.0 @aws-sdk/client-s3@3.620.0 @aws-sdk/client-ses@3.620.0 @aws-sdk/client-cognito-identity-provider@3.620.0 @aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner@3.620.0`

Step 2 — Replace c:\Users\laksh\OneDrive\Attachments\Desktop\LumaPath\.gitignore with the following content (each entry on its own line): node_modules/, .next/, .env.local, .env*.local, *.pem, .vercel/, coverage/

Step 3 — Create c:\Users\laksh\OneDrive\Attachments\Desktop\LumaPath\.env.local.example with every required environment variable and placeholder values: AWS_REGION=ap-south-1, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your_access_key_here, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your_secret_key_here, DYNAMODB_TABLE_NAME=MoiSubmissions, S3_BUCKET_NAME=lumapath-receipts, SES_FROM_EMAIL=noreply@lumapath.com, SES_REPLY_TO=support@lumapath.com, ADMIN_SECRET=your_secure_admin_password_here, NEXTAUTH_SECRET=your_nextauth_secret_here, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://digital-moi-express.vercel.app

Step 4 — Create c:\Users\laksh\OneDrive\Attachments\Desktop\LumaPath\lib\dynamodb.ts. Export a getDynamoClient() function that returns a DynamoDBDocumentClient (from @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb) configured with region process.env.AWS_REGION ?? 'ap-south-1', using process.env.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and process.env.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. If AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID is falsy return null — do not throw. Export DYNAMODB_TABLE_NAME = process.env.DYNAMODB_TABLE_NAME ?? 'MoiSubmissions'. Export a Submission interface: { transactionId: string; name: string; address: string; phone: string; amount: number; allocation: 'Both' | 'Bride' | 'Groom'; paymentMode: string; timestamp: string; event: string; }. Export putSubmission(submission: Submission): Promise<void> that wraps PutCommand in try/catch and no-ops if getDynamoClient() returns null. Export getSubmissions(): Promise<Submission[]> that wraps ScanCommand with Limit 1000, sorts descending by timestamp, returns [] on error or null client. Export getSubmissionById(transactionId: string): Promise<Submission | null> that uses GetCommand with Key {transactionId}.

Step 5 — Create c:\Users\laksh\OneDrive\Attachments\Desktop\LumaPath\lib\s3.ts. Export uploadReceiptToS3(transactionId: string, pngBuffer: Buffer): Promise<string | null> that uses @aws-sdk/client-s3 PutObjectCommand, bucket from process.env.S3_BUCKET_NAME ?? 'lumapath-receipts', key receipts/{transactionId}.png, ContentType image/png. Wrap in try/catch, return the S3 URL on success (https://{bucket}.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/receipts/{transactionId}.png) or null on error. Return null immediately if AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID is falsy.

Step 6 — Create c:\Users\laksh\OneDrive\Attachments\Desktop\LumaPath\lib\ses.ts. Import SESClient and SendEmailCommand from @aws-sdk/client-ses. Export sendReceiptEmail(submission: Submission): Promise<void> (import Submission from lib/dynamodb.ts). The function builds an HTML email with LumaPath branding (violet header, receipt table, emerald footer) and sends it via SESClient using SES_FROM_EMAIL env var as Source. Recipient is extracted from submission.phone as a placeholder (the function accepts an optional email param: sendReceiptEmail(submission, toEmail?: string), skip sending if toEmail is falsy). Wrap entirely in try/catch — never throw. Return immediately (no-op) if AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or SES_FROM_EMAIL env vars are falsy.

Step 7 — Create c:\Users\laksh\OneDrive\Attachments\Desktop\LumaPath\lib\cognito.ts. This file implements a simple ADMIN_SECRET-based password check (no actual Cognito user pool calls needed for the prototype). Export verifyAdminPassword(password: string): boolean that returns password === (process.env.ADMIN_SECRET ?? ''). Export generateSessionToken(): string that returns a base64-encoded JSON {iat: Date.now(), exp: Date.now() + 86400000} — this is a lightweight token for the httpOnly cookie. Export verifySessionToken(token: string): boolean that decodes the base64 JSON, checks exp > Date.now(). Import CognitoIdentityProviderClient from @aws-sdk/client-cognito-identity-provider at the top of the file (typed import only, to satisfy the package installation requirement), but do not instantiate it unless process.env.COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID is set.
acceptance_criteria: npm install exits 0 and all 6 @aws-sdk packages appear in package.json dependencies
.env.local.example exists with all 10 environment variable keys
lib/dynamodb.ts, lib/s3.ts, lib/ses.ts, lib/cognito.ts all exist with correct TypeScript exports
npm run build exits 0 with no TypeScript errors from the lib files

Run `npm run build` from c:\Users\laksh\OneDrive\Attachments\Desktop\LumaPath — must exit 0 (CI has no real AWS creds; lib files must not throw at import time)
findings: All 6 @aws-sdk packages installed at exact version 3.620.0. lib/ directory created with 4 files. Exported signatures: getDynamoClient()->DynamoDBDocumentClient|null, putSubmission(Submission)->Promise<void>, getSubmissions()->Promise<Submission[]>, getSubmissionById(transactionId)->Promise<Submission|null>, DYNAMODB_TABLE_NAME:string (lib/dynamodb.ts). uploadReceiptToS3(transactionId,pngBuffer)->Promise<string|null> (lib/s3.ts). sendReceiptEmail(submission,toEmail?)->Promise<void> (lib/ses.ts). verifyAdminPassword(password)->boolean, generateSessionToken()->string, verifySessionToken(token)->boolean, getCognitoClient()->CognitoIdentityProviderClient|null (lib/cognito.ts). All functions guard on AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and return null/no-op when missing, allowing CI build without real credentials. npm run lint and npm run build both exit 0. Commit: ed91d13 on master.
